history.dynasty: Founded by Madhvacharya; patronised by Vijayanagara, Keladi Nayaka and Mysore Wodeyar rulers
history.summary: The Sri Krishna Matha is the central institution of the Dvaita Vedanta school, founded by the Vaishnavite saint Madhvacharya (1238-1317 CE) in the 13th century. According to the founding legend, Madhvacharya rescued a storm-hit ship near Malpe beach and recovered an idol of Krishna embedded in a lump of gopichandana (sandalwood paste) given by the grateful ship's captain; the idol, said to have been sculpted by Vishwakarma from saligrama stone and worshipped at Dwaraka, was installed at Udupi. Installed facing east, the deity is said to have turned west (Pashchimabhimukha) in response to the devotion of Kanakadasa, who was denied entry and prayed from the western side — devotees still view the deity through the silver-plated nine-holed window (Navagraha Kindi) and the outer Kanakana Kindi. Madhvacharya founded eight monasteries (Ashta Mathas — Pejavara, Puttige, Palimaru, Adamaru, Sodhe, Kaniyooru, Shirur, Krishnapura) to care for the temple, rotating its management every two years in the Paryaya system, which completed 500 years in 2021. Vijayanagara kings, Keladi Nayakas and the Wodeyars patronised it; the matha remains one of the holiest Vaishnavite centres in South India and a hub of Dasa Sahitya.

name: Sri Krishna Matha
town_description: Udupi is a coastal city in Tulu Nadu, Karnataka, best known as the birthplace of the Dvaita school of Vedanta and home to the famous Sri Krishna Matha. It is a major pilgrimage city whose temple streets draw lakhs of devotees, and it is also famous nationwide for Udupi vegetarian cuisine. Malpe beach lies about 6 km away, and the city is well connected by rail and road to Mangaluru and Bengaluru.

travel.road: Well connected by KSRTC and private buses on NH-66 from Mangaluru (~60 km) and Bengaluru (~400 km) (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Paryaya (January, biennial) and Sri Krishna Janmashtami draw the largest crowds
